item: The scheduler's pass-tail briefing refresh (oo-briefing-bg) writes the cache where it started
summary: BackgroundScheduler._refresh_briefing_async resolves the cache file once, before the oo-briefing-bg thread exists (service.cache_path_for_a_new_run), and the thread runs refresh_briefing inside service.pinned_cache_path(path), the same ContextVar mechanism service._bg_refresh uses since #1596, so every cache read and write of that run goes to the folder it started in (before: data_dir() at each use, so a refresh that outlived its test or ran while the data folder changed wrote briefing_cache.json elsewhere). A cache folder that cannot be resolved starts nothing and frees the lock taken just before (a held lock would have made every later pass skip the refresh as still running). Tests (tests/test_briefing_scheduler_pin.py, 4 tests in 5 cases): the cache resolves to the start folder when OO_DATA_DIR moves mid-run (red with the pin removed), the pin does not outlive the run or reach the caller, an unresolvable folder frees the lock (red with the release removed). Stated: the hunk is inside _refresh_briefing_async, not stop()/start()/resume_after_exclusive_operation; _bg_refresh was left as it is (it sets the ContextVar directly, not through pinned_cache_path); not measured: how long a real rebuild takes.
